title: make_link_local accepts zone string 0 that integer path rejects
description:
## Problem

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py _normalize_zone_id() documents that zero cannot identify an owning interface. Integer 0 and negatives raise AddrError. The string path only rejects empty, '%', and whitespace.

Verified against stdlib IPv6Address:

- make_link_local(bytes(8), zone_id=0) -> AddrError
- make_link_local(bytes(8), zone_id='0') -> IPv6Address('fe80::%0')
- make_link_local(bytes(8), zone_id='00') -> IPv6Address('fe80::%00')
- make_link_local(bytes(8), zone_id='-1') -> IPv6Address('fe80::%-1')
- make_link_local(bytes(8), zone_id='\\x00') -> IPv6Address with a NUL scope_id

RFC 4007 zone index 0 is the unspecified/default zone. Callers that stringify an ifindex (str(0)) bypass the guard. test_assignment_rejects_invalid_zones covers 0 and -1 as ints, not their decimal strings.

## Why it matters

Zone is local send metadata (hhfc). A default-zone or NUL zone on a link-local used for LCI bind/send is not an owning interface. The public boundary claims to reject that and does not.

## Where

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:128-148 _normalize_zone_id
python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:151-171 make_link_local
python/tests/ipv6/test_link_local_assignment.py:74-77
design: _normalize_zone_id should treat the decimal spelling of a rejected index the same as the integer. After the string-type check, reject zone_id that is all ASCII digits and int(zone_id) <= 0 (covers '0', '00', '-1'). Also reject ASCII control characters (ord < 32 or 127), matching the existing %/whitespace filter. Keep real interface names ('lci0', 'eth0') and positive indexes.
acceptance_criteria: make_link_local(iid, zone_id=0), zone_id='0', zone_id='00', and zone_id='-1' all raise AddrError. zone_id='\x00' raises AddrError. zone_id=7, '7', 'lci0' still attach that scope_id and do not change .packed. Existing test_assignment_rejects_invalid_zones cases stay green.
